FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Third Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 November 1984, after the draft finalized by the Petroleum Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Cduncil. 0.2 This standard was originally published in 1960 and revised in 1967 and 1976. This third revision has been prepared as a result of a review of the standard in the light of the present day requirements of the product and in order to align it with specification No. D. Eng. R. D. 2498 ` Turbine fuel, aviation, high flash type `, issued by the (issue 7), Ministry of Defence, UK, which is currently in use. The committee had also decided to adopt JFTOT method in place of the existing CFR Coker method for the determination of thermal stability which has been introduced in this ,revision accordingly. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, `he final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for aviation turbine fuels, high flash point type, used in turboprop and jer-engined aircrafts. 2. REQUIREMENTS 2.1 General - The material shall be clear, bright and free from undissolved water, and solid matter at normal ambient temperature.
*Rules for round@ off numerical valum ( rabid ) .

3

IS t 1587 - 1984 2.1.1 The material shall possess satisfactory good performance when used in appropriate or both. properties and shall Five aircraft or aeroengmes

2.2 Composition - The material shall consist completely of hydrocarbon compounds, except the materials specified in 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.4 and 2.2.5. 2.2.1 Antioxidants 2.2.1.1 Fuels which have been ` hydrogen treated ' - An approved antioxidant, or mixture of antioxidants, shall be added at the appropriate time during manufacture in order to prevent gum formation and peroxiThe total mass of active materials shall be not dation after manufacture. less than 17.0 mg/l nor more than 24.0 mg/l. 2.2.1.2 Fuels which have not been ` hydrogen treated ' - An approved antioxidant, or mixture of antioxidants, may be added at the appropriate time during manufacttire in order to prevent gum formation after manufacture. The total mass of active material(s) shall not exceed 24.0 mg/l. 2.2.1.3 The following are the approved antioxidants:

a) 2, 6-ditertiary-butyl-phenol; b) 2, 6-ditertiary-butyl-4-methyl-phenol; c) 2, 4-dimethyl-6-tertiary-butyl-phenol; d) 75 percent, Min, 2, 6-ditertiary-butyl-phenols; and e) 25 percent, Max, tertiary and tritertiary-butyl-phenols;

f ) 55 percent, Min, 2, 4-dimethyl-6-tertiary-butyl-phenol; 15 percent, Min, 4-methyl-2, 6-ditertiary-butyl-phenol; with the remainder a mixture of monomethyl and dimethyltertiary-butyl-phenols. 2.2.1.4 These antioxidants have wide and long standing usage. Other Substituted phenols, and mixture thereof, are known to be equally effective. The use of alternative materials requires Design Authority consent ( declaration of composition and evidence of satisfactory performance will normally be necessary ). 2.2.2 Metal Deactivator - An approved metal deactivator may be added in amounts not exceeding 5.7 ms/l of active ingredient. The approved metal deactivator is N, N-disalicyhdene, 1, 2-propanediamine. 2.2.3 The supplier shall, if required by the purchaser or his authorized agent, disclose the nature and concentration respectively of gum inhibitor and metal deactivator which have been added to his fuel supplies. 4

IS t 1587- 1984 2.2.4 Corrosion Inhibitor - If agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, an approved corrosion inhibitor may be added to the fuel. Edwin cooper additive Hitec E 5 15 ( Santolene C ) is an approved corrosion inhibitor which may be added at the time of delivery to the purchaser, The Hitec E 515 shall in a concentration between Il.4 to 14.3 mgll. comply in all respect with the requirements given in Table 1.

B-1.1 This method describes a procedure for the detection siveness of aviation turbine fuels towards silver. B-2. OUTLINE OF THE METHOD

B-2.1 A polished silver strip is completely immersed in 1 litre of fuel at 45�C f 1�C for a period of 16 hours, or any longer period which may be specified. At the end of this period, the silver strip is removed from
the sample, washed, and evaluated for corrosion. 11

SUPPORTPORSILVER STRIP

B-5. PREPARATION

OF STRIPS

- Remove all surface blemishes from all six sides of the strip with silicon carbide or alumina grit paper sufficiently fine to accomplish the desired results ( see Note ). Finish with 240 grit silicon carbide paper or No. 00 emery cloth, or its equivalent, removing all marks that may have been made by other grades of paper used previously. Immerse the strip in &octane, from which it may be withdrawn when proceeding to the final polishing strip.
NOTE- As a practical manual procedure for surface preparation, place a sheet of the abrasive paper on a flat surface, moisten it with to-octane, and rub the

B-5.1 Surface Preparation

strip against the paper with a rotary motion, protecting the strip from contact with Alternatively, the strip may be prepared the fingers with an ashless filter-paper. mechanically, uring appropriate grades of dry paper or cloth.

13

IS:1587-1984 B-5.2 Final Polishing - Remove a strip from Go-octane. Holding it in the fingers protected with ashless filter paper, polish first the ends and then the sides with the 106-micron silicon carbide grains prcked up from a clean glass plate with a pad of cotton wool moistened with a drop of &-octane. Wipe vigorously with fresh pads of absorbent cotton and subsequently handle only with stainless steel forceps; DO NOT TOUCH WITH THE FINGERS. Clamp in the vice and polish the main surfaces with the silicon carbide grains on absorbent cotton. Rub in the direction of the long axis of the strip, carrying the stroke beyond the end of the strip before reversing Clean all metal dust from the strip by rubbing vigorously the direction. with clean pads of absorbent cotton until a fresh pad remains unsoiled. Immerse the strip in the sample within 1 minute of completing the final polishing.
NOTE - It is important to polish the whole surface of the strip uniformly to obtain a uniformly stained strip. If the edges show wear ( surface eliptical ) they are The use of a vice facilitates uniform likely to show more corrosion than the centre. polishing.

B-6.

SAMPLE

B-6.1 It is particularly important that care is taken during sampling and subsequent handling to eliminate aeration of the sample and to protect them from exposure to direct or even diffused daylight. Samples of 1 litre minimum size shall be collected in containers which will not affect the corrosion properties of the fuels ( see Note ). Clean dark brown bottles are preferred. Fill the container to leave not more than 5 percent ullage and close it immediately after taking the sample. Store the sample in a cool Test the sample as soon as possible after place, preferably below 4�C. receipt and immediately after opening the container.
NOTE 1 Experience has showa that tinplate containers are particularly this respect. bad in

B-6.2 If suspended water ( haze ) is observed in the sample ( see Note ), filter through a medium rapid quantitative filter paper ( for example, Whatman No. 1 or No. 4 ) into the clean, dry flask. Carry out this operation in a.darkened room or under a light protected shield.
NOTE - Contact of the silver strip with water before, during or after completion of the test run, will cause staining, making it difficult to evaluate the strip.

B-7.

PROCEDURE

B-7.1 Pour 1 litre of the sample into the clean conical flask. Fit the Insert a freshly polished strip into condenser to the flask ( see Note ). the support or, alternatively, suspend it vertically by means of a nylon thread loop. Carefully lower the strip into the sample.
cork may be substituted

THERMAL ALCOR OXIDATION STABILITY OF ATF BY JET FUEL THERMAL OXIDATION TESTER ( JFTOT METHOD)

C-l.

GENERAL

9.1.6.1 In rating the heater tube the darkest code number representative of the darkest section deposit, shall be reported.

9.1.6.2 If a spot or streak is found on the heater tube, it shall be examined carrfully under various lighting conditions using a magnfying glass to determine if it is a deposit a scratch or a tube defect ( noti that any tube defects; should have been found during the pre-test inspection of the tube ). If the spot or streak is detc rmined to be a scratch or tube defczct, it shall be disregarded. It the spot or streak is a deposit, it shall be rated against the ASTM Colour Standards if larger in area than about 2.5 mm*, that is approximately l-5 mm* or an equivalent area. However, a streak deposit shall be ignored if less than O-8 mm wide, regardless of length.
NOTE - Since the tube test section is about 3 mm in diameter; thus a 1.5 mm wide spot is l/2 the diameter of the tube test section and a 0'8 mm wide streak is l/4 diameter of the tube test section.
